name: An Assembly Of Birds
intro: In this chapter, we'll build some more real-life like functions from combinators.
This is going to be tedious. Brace yourself!
Throughout this chapter, unless specified otherwise, the following conventions apply:
cons = V = x->y->f x y, nil = KI (linked lists / pairs),
and lst = head->tail->f->x->f head (tail f x) (self-folding list, also nil-terminated).

content.name: Hello World
intro: Given lst and nil, return a list of ASCII character codes
Key codes for letters start with A = 65, code for space is 32.
Numeric literals are NOT allowed, you'll have to construct them all!

content.name: Read binary
intro: Given a linked list of true/false values,
return a Church numeral representing the binary number stored in the list, little endian.
E.g. (cons false (cons true (cons true nil))) should return 6.
Usual conventions apply: cons = V = x->y->f x y, nil = KI,
